updates.body: We are investigating delays of up to 20 minutes in webhook deliveries.
A delivery queue node failed over and a backlog formed behind it. We have added capacity and the backlog is draining.
Deliveries are back to normal latency. Queued events are being delivered in order; none were dropped.

incident.title: Pipeline jobs queued longer than usual
incident.markdown:
## Impact

For 2 hours 45 minutes, about one in five pipeline jobs on hosted Linux runners waited more than ten minutes to start. Jobs on self-hosted runners were not affected, and no job results were lost.

## Timeline

1. 14:02 UTC — queue times begin to rise in one region
2. 14:19 UTC — alert fires; investigation starts
3. 15:10 UTC — a faulty runner image is identified and rolled back
4. 16:47 UTC — queue times back to normal

## What caused it

A new runner image failed its health check after boot, so runners were created and torn down in a loop instead of taking jobs.

## What we changed

Runner images now roll out to one region at a time and stop automatically when boot health checks fail.

updates.body: We are investigating longer than usual queue times for pipeline jobs on hosted runners.
We have traced the delay to a runner image released this afternoon and are rolling it back.
The rollback is complete and queued jobs are starting. We are watching queue times recover.
Queue times are back to normal. A full write-up is attached to this incident.
Some users are seeing connection resets when pushing or fetching over SSH. HTTPS is not affected. We are investigating.
A configuration change to our SSH load balancers caused the resets. We are reverting it.
The change has been reverted and SSH connections are succeeding again.

incident.title: Scheduled maintenance for the package registry
incident.markdown: We are upgrading the database behind the package registry. Publishing new versions may be paused for up to ten minutes during the window. Installs and downloads are not affected.
